## Command Details

```text
Manage rebuildable read-only projections (ADR-0019 D5; ADR-0012 amendment):
Governance Graph, Governed Knowledge Base, and Visualization Workbench.
Projections are derived from canonical Amber artifacts and are never canonical
authority — rebuild() regenerates from canonical state at any time.

Subcommands:
  rebuild --type <governance-graph|knowledge-base|visualization-workbench>
        Rebuild from canonical artifacts: context pages (.amber/context/pages/),
        plus committed Canonical Artifact revisions for the Governance Graph.
  status --type <type>  Report projection state: missing, current, or drifted.
  strict-query --scope <node> --checkpoint <sha256> --projection-version 1
        --limit <n> --sort id --depth <0|1> [--cursor <cursor>]
        Strict Governance Graph read: exact scope/checkpoint/version,
        expiring cursor, and stale dependency refusal.
  invalidate --subject <scope> --dependency <type:identity[@revision]> --reason <text>
        Append a scoped staleness receipt; history is never rewritten.
  list                  List all projections and their status.

Examples:
  amber projection rebuild --type governance-graph --target . --json
  amber projection status --type knowledge-base --target . --json
```

## Examples

```bash
amber projection rebuild --type governance-graph --target . --json
```


## Boundaries & Safety

- `--target <path>` selects repository state. Amber confines these target-relative paths, refusing `..` and symlink escapes before reading or writing: plan and scaffold destinations (including `accept --plan`), memory and context payloads, harness inputs, adapter allow-lists, workflow reports and their output directory, ledger exports, execution readiness plans, session and worktree state, governance report output, wiki export and handoff bundle output directories.
- Path validation is not OS sandboxing, and the confinement above covers only the surfaces it names, and a confined flag still accepts an absolute destination only when it stays inside the target. `governance audit --output`, `governance readiness --output`, `security audit --output`, `loop record --output`, and `explain --markdown` resolve against the working directory instead of `--target`. A path flag not listed here is confined only when the command that reads it routes through the boundary. A governed or verification command still runs with your user's file permissions.
- `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, and `workflow assess` reject output directories that resolve to the target root, including `.`, an absolute root path, `nested/..`, and symlink or junction aliases of the root. Output subdirectories and defaults are unchanged.
- `wiki export` and `handoff bundle` check all planned file destinations and their parent directories before the first write, including copied wiki pages and optional replay files. An existing child symlink, junction, or hard link outside the target refuses the export without changing output files. A link to another path inside the target is still written through, so it replaces that file's bytes; a planned leaf hard-linked to another name is refused instead. Concurrent link replacement is not prevented.
- `handoff validate --bundle-dir .` and `workflow assess --handoff-bundle-dir .` still accept root-level bundles as read-only inputs. Explicit handoff validation paths outside `--target` are refused.
- **Fail-Closed Behavior**: Corrupt governance state or invalid schema parameters immediately halt execution with non-zero exit codes.
